Quotes / Lucretius / Q0043

Therefore death is nothing to us, and does not concern us at all.
Thinker Lucretius
School Epicureanism
Source De Rerum Natura III.830
Theme Death
Another quotation More from this thinker

Context and commentary are editorial aids for reading. They do not replace the primary text or scholarly commentary.

Source context

This English passage is associated with De Rerum Natura III.830, within the tradition of Epicureanism. The wording below is a verified rendering prepared for careful reading rather than a claim of unique translation authority.

A short reading

Read in the register of death, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Lucretius's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
